title: Shall We Go on to Sin
description: Shall We Go on to Sin in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 106, headed “Dead to sin by the cross of Christ, Rom. 6. 1 2 6”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Shall we go on to sin Be-cause thy grace a-bounds, Or cru-ci-fy the Lord a-gain, And o-pen all his wounds?

lines: Shall we go on to sin
Nor let it e'er be said
That we whose sins are crucify'd
Should raise them from the dead.
We will be slaves no more,
Since Christ has made us free,
Has nail'd our tyrants to his cross,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
